premises.logline: Every Sunday Juno and her droopy plant have a silent standoff over the watering can; one capful ends the guessing for both of them.
premises.productRole: The capful replaces her water-and-hope guessing with one clear routine.
premises.hookIdea: A woman and a plant staring each other down, title card 'Sunday standoff'.

premises.logline: A new flat-sitter inherits a windowsill of plants and a note that just says 'feed them'; Sprigly's label is the only instruction that makes sense.
premises.productRole: The dose on the label turns a vague note into a plan.
premises.hookIdea: A sticky note: 'feed them.' Feed them WHAT?

premises.logline: Two flatmates argue about how much plant food is 'a bit'; the measuring cap settles it.
premises.productRole: One capful per litre ends the argument.
premises.hookIdea: 'A splash.' 'A glug.' Two people, one plant, no agreement.

premises.logline: An office plant everyone forgets is adopted by the intern, who sets a fortnightly reminder and a capful.
premises.productRole: A routine simple enough to keep at work.
premises.hookIdea: A plant on a desk with a name tag nobody reads.

premises.logline: A grandad who 'just knows' plants teaches his grandson the old way, and the grandson shows him the cap that measures it.
premises.productRole: It writes down what grandad does by feel.
premises.hookIdea: 'You feel it in your thumb.' Close-up of a green thumb.

premises.logline: A plant narrates its own life in a flat: two weeks of hopeful glances at the owner until feeding day finally comes.
premises.productRole: It gives the owner a day to remember: feeding day.
premises.hookIdea: POV of a plant: 'Day 14. Still waiting.'

premises.logline: A busy nurse coming off night shifts only has thirty seconds for her plants; one capful fits.
premises.productRole: A thirty-second routine that fits a hard week.
premises.hookIdea: A clock at 7:02 am and a coat still on.

premises.logline: A café owner's window plants look tired in the photos customers post; she starts a fortnightly feeding ritual before opening.
premises.productRole: A routine she can hand to staff: one capful per litre.
premises.hookIdea: A phone photo of a café window, zoom to the sad plant in the corner.

premises.logline: A man buys a plant to prove he can look after something, then realises he doesn't know how; the bottle tells him in one line.
premises.productRole: The one-line dose makes care feel doable.
premises.hookIdea: 'I can keep a plant alive.' He can't. Yet.

premises.logline: A child asks why the plant looks sad; the parent, unsure, finds the answer on a bottle and they make feeding day their thing.
premises.productRole: A clear routine a parent can share.
premises.hookIdea: 'Is the plant sad?' A small voice, a big question.

output.reason: The Sunday standoff fits in one look: a tired person and a tired plant face to face. It has one emotion, relief, and the turn comes from Sprigly's honest benefit, one capful and no guessing, not from a miracle. It all happens on a kitchen windowsill, which the kit draws well. The flatmates' argument (p3) is the runner-up and would make a good second ad.
